news.title: Alonso on learning from every game, win or lose
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes Sunday’s loss to Arsenal will prove to be an important part of the learning process as his Chelsea team continues to take shape during the early stages of his tenure as manager. The Blues travelled across the capital for a London derby away at title holders Arsenal in our third Premier League fixture under Alonso’s leadership. Morgan Rogers gave us an early lead in a good start at the Emirates Stadium, but the Gunners came back to win 2-1, even if we went close to further goals when Pedro Neto hit the post and Estevao Willian had a late shot tipped over the bar. The Chelsea manager felt we showed we are on the right track by taking the game to last season’s champions and pushing them all the way in their stadium, even if there are still areas where improvement is needed. ‘I want to compete in the best possible way to win,’ explained Alonso after the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium. ‘Yesterday, we didn’t want to from the first minute sit deep and to wait and to make it a long game. We wanted to be active. We wanted to be protagonists in the pressing – sometimes to go higher, sometimes lower – to have good possession. ‘We did many things right, other things we need to make better. We need to learn from them, because this is the top level and when we have to play at the top level we want to be as efficient and as accurate in all the phases of the game as possible. ‘But this is where we are. This is game three for us in this new start, this new phase for Chelsea, but I am happy with the spirit and attitude of the players. They have given everything, they have tried and they fought really hard.’ As Alonso points out, it is still early days for the Blues under our Spanish manager, meaning every game is an opportunity to continue learning and improving. ‘Yesterday’s game, we will take many things for the next one, as we have done so far after Fulham, after Brighton, after Luton. We want to squeeze everything from each game to make things better, when we win and when we lose as well. ‘That is the process of where we are, where we want to build strong principles and strong ideas for our game, little by little, to win games and to compete in the best possible way.’

news.title: Full Match: Arsenal vs Chelsea
Extended: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea
Morgan Rogers: We know we will get even better
news.body_en: Three victories did not convince Morgan Rogers that Chelsea were the finished article. One defeat has not altered his belief in where they are heading. Sunday’s 2-1 loss at Arsenal was the first setback of Xabi Alonso’s tenure, but Rogers’ message remained the same as it would have been had the Blues left north London with another victory. It is still early. There is still work to do. And there is no doubt in the forward’s mind that Chelsea will continue to improve. ‘It’s only the fourth game under him,’ said Rogers. ‘We know we’ve got work to do. Even after the three wins, we knew work was needed, so it doesn’t change. We stay fully focused and move forward. ‘We work hard on the training pitch, trying to understand each other more and how we want to play. We’ll get better. We know we will. ‘We’ll be here again, having the same conversation about improving because we always want to improve and always will get better.’ That conviction has been strengthened by the positive start Alonso has made at Cobham and the speed with which the squad have embraced his ideas. That has been evidenced by the Blues heading into today's London derby off the back of three victories against Fulham, Brighton & Hove Albion and Luton Town in the Carabao Cup. ‘It’s been really good and really positive,’ Rogers continued. ‘You see time and time again that managers come in and struggle at the start when they are adapting, but we have done really well to take the manager’s ideas on board. ‘We have used our quality and the players we have in the changing room. We have done well to win the games we have and with the way we have played. ‘Of course, there are areas to improve because it is really early days. But seeing the positive signs so early and being encouraged constantly, every day on the training pitch and in games, there is only one way we are going – and that is forward. ‘That is all you can ask as a player when there has been a change in the building and you are trying to achieve something.’ That longer-term optimism did not lessen the immediate frustration felt by Rogers and his team-mates at the final whistle in north London. It was Rogers who had put Chelsea in front inside the opening two minutes with his arrowed shot into the bottom corner from the edge of the penalty area. But Kai Havertz pulled a goal back midway thorough the first half and Martin Odegaard's finish early into the second period proved to be enough, despite the Blues going in search of an equaliser, with Estevao Willian in particular bringing the best out of David Raya. ‘We are disappointed,’ he acknowledged. ‘We came here with a job to try to win, and we didn’t manage that, so of course the players and the boys are disappointed. But it’s a long season and it’s a tough place to come. ‘I think we gave a good account of ourselves. We played well in large parts of the game, created chances and defended well when we had to. Of course, it’s tough, and they’re in a really good moment right now and feeling really good. ‘There is still stuff for us to work on. We’re still new, with a new manager, trying to combine our ideas and get better and better. But we will. We know we will. ‘We know we’ve got the quality in the room. It’s just about working hard on the training field and putting things right.’

news.title: Highlights: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea
'I liked the spirit and the fight'
'We went toe-to-toe with them'
Match gallery: Blues edged out at Arsenal
Alonso: Arsenal loss needs to hurt in a positive way
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso was proud of his Chelsea side's fighting spirit against Arsenal and hopes the pain of defeat will fuel the Blues as the season progresses. We acquitted ourselves well at the Emirates Stadium, going toe-to-toe with the Premier League title holders and taking an early lead when Morgan Rogers fired home a fine volley inside the first two minutes. Arsenal fought back to take the lead themselves after half-time, but Chelsea pushed the Gunners all the way, with Pedro Neto striking the post and Estevao Willian being spectacularly denied by goalkeeper David Raya late on. As he assessed the game after the final whistle, Alonso insisted that as disappointing as any defeat is, he was proud of the battling qualities shown by his team in this London derby. ‘It was a game with different stages of momentum,' said the Blues manager. 'We started the game well, scoring first, and the next 15 minutes they were really pushing us hard. We were defending low, struggling to have a little bit more of the ball to play a little bit more on the pitch. ‘So those 15 minutes were hard and we had to suffer. Once we conceded the goal for 1-1, the game came back to an even level for them and from us. We had a couple of good chances before the end of the first half, but at half-time we spoke. 'It was a very close game, very intense, when we had to have really high levels of concentration, not to give many advantages to them to be in the game, to be fighting for it. 'For sure, the second goal, we could’ve done a little bit better. It’s a part of the game you need to accept because they are a top side and they push you to the limits. They overload a lot on the left side with many players and they got the goal with Odegaard. 'But after that we have kept going and the team showed really good desire and good spirit to fight until the end. We were close with the chance from Este. 'It’s a defeat and we are disappointed; it needs to hurt, but it needs to hurt in a positive way because it’s just game three [of the season]. There are still many games to play and we knew it was going to be a very intense game today.' The Spaniard was also asked after the game if there were any new concerns over Moises Caicedo missing the trip to Arsenal - having been forced off on his return from injury against Brighton & Hove Albion last week - as well as what impact being without the Ecuadorian and Levi Colwill had on Sunday's game. 'It is not long-term [for Caicedo] but it’s about assessing the risk,' added Alonso. 'Probably, last week, we took him too early and I don’t want to make the same mistake again. 'It’s easy after defeats to talk about the players that you are missing. I’m not going to go there, I am happy with the players that we have. 'For sure, all the managers need to deal with injuries, with suspensions. To have all the players available for all the games is impossible. But we need [Caicedo and Colwill] because they are top players and with them we are a better team.'

news.title: Match report: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea succumbed to a narrow defeat away at Premier League title holders Arsenal, despite the Blues taking another early lead at the Emirates Stadium. The Blues were eyeing a memorable afternoon in north London as we looked to end our derby rivals' 100 per cent record this season with a statement Premier League victory. We took a step towards that becoming reality when Morgan Rogers caught everyone out with a clever first-time shot from outside the box that wrong-footed goalkeeper David Raya on its way into the left-hand corner. Unfortunately, we couldn't hold that advantage, as Arsenal levelled before half-time through Kai Havertz. Martin Odegaard then broke free in the penalty area to give the home side a 2-1 lead shortly after the break. Chelsea refused to lie down and fought hard to salvage a share of the points, and were only denied it by a matter of inches after Pedro Neto hit the post and David Raya tipped an Estevao Willian shot over the bar, but it wasn't to be. Emi Martinez continued between the posts against the club that first brought him to England, but there was a change to the shape ahead of him. Josh Acheampong came in at right-back - Levi Colwill making way - French duo Wesley Fofana and Maxence Lacroix were in the middle, with Jorrel Hato dropping deeper at left-back. Reece James came in for Malo Gusto in midfield with Romeo Lavia, as Pedro Neto pushed higher on the right to join Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers in supporting striker Joao Pedro. There was a big atmosphere inside the Emirates Stadium come kick-off, as you would expect for a London derby between two teams who went into this game with 100 per cent records this season, both sets of supporters eagerly anticipating a massive Sunday afternoon Premier League fixture. Chelsea have made early goals a theme of our season so far, and it was another flying start from the Blues as we opened the scoring inside two minutes. It all stemmed from a free-kick, lofted into the Arsenal box by James and won in the air by Lacroix. It broke loose, but the Gunners failed to clear and Hato kept it alive – his header bouncing invitingly towards Rogers on the edge of the area. The England international didn’t need a second invitation, sweeping a first-time shot low and into the bottom corner, beyond the dive of Raya. The Blues were 1-0 up, but the job was far from done as the Gunners tried to hit back immediately. A free-kick of their own out wide was delivered low and caused chaos in a six-yard box scramble. Martinez was brave to save low and then delve into the tangle of limbs to put the ball out of danger, taking a boot to the head from Gabriel Magalhaes in the process. Dead-ball situations seemed to be the order of the day and Arsenal thought they had levelled the scores when another low free-kick came into the Chelsea box and caused chaos. In a frantic scramble, Martinez initially saved from Ezri Konsa, only for Gabriel’s follow-up to hit the post and squirm back across his goal out of reach, where Riccardo Calafiori was able to score from close range. However, VAR intervened with Konsa offside. Our lead was retained. We were having to work hard to keep it that way, as the home side pushed upfield and Martinez had to save from Havertz and Bukayo Saka, although neither effort really troubled him at his near post. Palmer and James tested Raya with efforts from outside the box, but Chelsea attacks were rare midway through the first half, as Arsenal tried to get back on level terms before the break. There was some stern defending, and one brilliant challenge by Hato in particular, as we tried to prevent them from doing so. Unfortunately, it wouldn’t last. The pressure eventually told when Havertz cut in from the right onto his left foot and found a yard to roll a shot inside Martinez’s near post from the edge of the box. All square again at the Emirates Stadium. The first half ended in something of a stalemate, with neither team able to turn spells of possession into serious pressure, although Neto did come close when he struck the base of the left-hand post with a low shot on the counter in stoppage time. As it was, both teams came out for the second half looking determined to break the deadlock and secure all three points. Despite plenty of fight by the Blues, it was Arsenal who found the next goal and took the lead when Havertz dummied to let a low cross run past him to Odegaard, who had the time and space to finish at close range. Chelsea refused to give in, with Palmer looking for opportunities to get on the attack quickly, although we also needed to guard against Arsenal counter-attacks now. Xabi Alonso turned to his bench in an attempt to give us more control and move the game into the home team's half; Malo Gusto and Pep Chavarria came on in place of Hato and Lavia. The same pattern continued. Palmer and Joao Pedro were looking lively and carrying our biggest threat, but Martinez had to be quick off his line to prevent Arsenal breakaways on a couple of occasions, and produced one brilliant reaction save to deny Saka as we pushed upfield and risked leaving our keeper exposed. Chelsea continued to increase the pressure and had the title holders pinned back in their own half for much of the final 15 minutes. Despite that pressure, plus the introduction of Estevao Willian and Danny Welbeck to bolster our attack, there was just no way through the Arsenal defence. Our winning start to the season was over - despite Estevao forcing a late fingertip save from Raya - but there were still positives for Xabi Alonso to take away from the Emirates, after we pushed the champions all the way on their own turf. Despite dropping points for the first time this season, Chelsea remain fourth in the Premier League table at this early stage in the campaign, three behind joint-leaders Arsenal and Manchester City, who have the last remaining 100 per cent records. Chelsea are back in action in midweek in the first of two games at Stamford Bridge in the coming days. That will be in the Carabao Cup when we host Leeds United in the third round, with kick-off at 8pm on Wednesday 9 September, before Hull City come to SW6 in the Premier League at 3pm on Saturday 12 September. news.title: Xabi Alonso on Levi Colwill change and Moises Caicedo absence against Arsenal
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says no risks have been taken over Moises Caicedo and Levi Colwill's fitness, with the former not included in the squad to face Arsenal and the latter named among the substitutes. Our third Premier League fixture of the campaign takes us across London to the Emirates Stadium and Alonso has made two alterations to the side that started last weekend’s win over Brighton & Hove Albion. One of those is in defence, with Josh Acheampong replacing Colwill in the back line, while Reece James steps into midfield in place of Malo Gusto. When asked in his pre-match media interview why the change in defence had been made, Alonso replied: ‘Fitness. Levi had a little thing during the week, so we wanted not to take a risk at this stage of the season.’ On Caicedo's absence from the matchday squad, the Blues manager added: ‘He was close but, as well, there is no point in taking too many risks at this moment. Maybe we went too early against Brighton [with his return], so we need to be cautious.’ The Blues have made a strong start to the campaign, with back-to-back victories recorded in the top flight. Arsenal, who won the title last season, have the same record after two matches and Alonso accepts today's contest will be a good test for his developing side. He said: 'We will see how it goes, but for sure, it’s game three for us in this new project that we are starting and we want to have a great game today.'

news.title: Arsenal vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: Fourth-placed Chelsea make the short trip north to Emirates Stadium to face an Arsenal team in second place as they defend their first Premier League title in 21 years. Sunday’s kick-off is 4.30pm local time, and a first win there since August 2021 would maintain the west Londoners’ 100 per cent start under Xabi Alonso. The close of the transfer window means the dreamtime is over and every club has the squad that must serve them for the next four months. The first test sees the metropolis’ most successful clubs meet for Chelsea’s second London derby of the season and Arsenal’s first. It hands Morgan Rogers an early chance to validate his preference for the blue half of the capital – he has never previously scored against this weekend’s hosts. This is also the period when the football week starts to fill up – though with no European fixtures, the world champions only have Wednesday’s Carabao Cup visit by Leeds in the midweek calendar. Arsenal’s latest attempt to win the Champions League – a trophy that has so far eluded them – starts at Napoli’s Maradona Stadium on Wednesday. Blues manager Xabi Alonso would love a repeat of his first encounter with the Gunners on his 23rd birthday in November 2004 – a 2-1 victory in which he banged in the opener. Ten years ago a new boss took his promising Chelsea side to Emirates early in the Premier League season. The first half was a write-off as the Blues shipped three without reply, but a tactical switch after the break became a sliding-doors moment. Antonio Conte’s change to a three-man backline led to a thrilling campaign that eventually brought the national title back to west London. That was also one of six seasons when the Blues won away to the defending champions of the Premier League – a 3-0 victory at Claudio Ranieri’s Leicester with Marcos Alonso accounting for two and Pedro the other. The Londoners had done the same against the Premier League’s maiden winners, Manchester Utd – and repeated the feat several times since. Shortly before the 1994 FA Cup final, a Gavin Peacock finish was enough to end United’s 34-game unbeaten home run. Three seasons later, the same opponents were beaten at Old Trafford, with a Michael Duberry header and Luca Vialli’s nutmeg contributing to a 2-1 success. And in December 2001, the Londoners’ dominant display earned a 3-0 victory at United – Mario Melchiot, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Eidur Gudjohnsen finding the net. In April 2010, champions and hosts United were again 2-1 victims – this time Joe Cole and Didier Drogba doing the damage for Carlo Ancelotti’s future title winners. And most recently, in March 2021, Mason Mount’s only goal at Anfield helped topple Liverpool’s crown. Chelsea are aiming to open the season with four successive victories on all fronts for the first time since our title-winning 2016/17 season. With 49 goals from 98 Premier League games, Cole Palmer is one off a half-century – Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink (84) and Diego Costa (85) are the only Blues players to have reached 50 in fewer than 100 matches. Arsenal’s run of nine unbeaten against the Blues in the Premier League is their best since 1995-2005. Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta are two of the four current Premier League managers who hail from the Basque region of Spain. (The others are Unai Emery and Andoni Iraola.) The last time Arsenal beat Man City 3-0 in the Community Shield was 2014 – but it was Chelsea who went on to win the Premier League. Chelsea have generated 1.9 or more expected goals before half-time in both league matches to date. The world champions claimed just 26 per cent of possession during last weekend’s 4-3 beating of Brighton – but 53 per cent of total shots (17/32). Joao Pedro has scored and set up goals in both opening league fixtures this season – the first player in the club’s history to do so. Morgan Rogers has created nine chances for team-mates so far this season – the most in the Premier League and the highest total by any Blues player in his first two appearances on record (since 2003/04). Sunday’s match was the 28th we have won 4-3 and the 11th in the Premier League era. Between 9 April 1960 and 4 September 1965, Chelsea won all six league visits to Arsenal’s former ground, Highbury, scoring three or more each time – 4-1, 4-1, 3-0, 4-2, 3-1 and 3-1.

news.title: London's Finest vs The Gunners 🔥
Xabi Alonso backs Reece James to become one of the world's best midfielders
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso knows exactly what it takes to become one of the world's greatest midfielders. So his belief that Chelsea captain Reece James can reach that level carries significant weight. During his playing days, few midfielders could influence games from the middle of the pitch like Alonso. He had an unrivalled range of passing, read the game expertly, and was the orchestrator in teams that won league titles, the Champions League, European Championships, and the World Cup. Naturally, the tactical demands on midfielders have evolved since Alonso hung up his boots in 2017. Yet the qualities and attributes needed to thrive remain similar – and the Chelsea manager believes James has these in abundance. The 26-year-old also brings leadership and connection; James, a boyhood fan, is now into his fourth season as captain. The sight of the England international in the Chelsea midfield is nothing new. It's where he started as we defeated Paris Saint-Germain in the Club World Cup and a position he starred in last term in a game against Arsenal, today's opponents at the Emirates Stadium. And it was before our trip to north London that Alonso was asked whether James, one of the best right-backs in world football, could achieve the same status in midfield. ‘I would say so,' the Blues manager replied. 'He is very comfortable and confident playing in that position. He has the intelligence to play there because, in the middle, you need to be able to connect with your team-mates and know what the best thing to do is before you get the ball. 'He has this awareness. I remember him playing very, very well playing in the middle. So we are using him and he will have a lot of minutes as a midfielder.’ Alonso added: ‘For me, physically, when he is fresh and prepared, he has shown he can compete in the Premier League – no issue. 'As a midfielder, you have to take a lot of easy decisions and many right decisions. You are very connected to the game and are close to the action. Walking is not possible. 'So Reece is very involved in the game and knows where he needs to be. He has the capacity to help the team-mates around him and that is very important to me because he has this presence where he has respect from his teammates. When he says something, they listen and they follow him.' In our opening three matches of the campaign, Alonso has used several different midfield combinations. James was partnered by Lavia against Fulham and then featured alongside Valentin Barco in our Carabao Cup win over Luton Town. Last time out, against Brighton and Hove Albion, James stepped out of the side and it was left to Lavia and Malo Gusto to hold down the middle of the pitch. ‘You plan the squad knowing the profiles you have and some players can play in different positions,' Alonso explained. 'Reece can play in the middle, and Malo Gusto can play in the middle and other positions as well. We look at the squad and feel we are good to go. 'If we have injuries and suspensions, we feel we will be able to manage. So that is why we feel we are in a good position.'

news.title: The Arsenal and Chelsea connections: Who has played for both clubs?
news.body_en: Chelsea versus Arsenal is a London derby which first took place in 1907 so it will come as no surprise that quite a few players have featured for both teams over the years. Here we look at some of those to have worn the blue and red during the Premier League era. To qualify for this list, a player must have made a competitive senior appearance for both clubs and must no longer play for either. That excludes current Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez, as well as Arsenal trio Kepa Arrizabalaga, Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke. Cech is a certified Chelsea legend, having played for the club between 2004 and 2015. He won four Premier Leagues, four FA Cups, three League Cups, and both the Champions League and Europa League. The former Czechia international is widely considered to be one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation and after transferring to Arsenal in 2015, he became a fans' favourite at the Emirates too during his final four seasons as a player, whilst also adding an FA Cup to his collection. Cech returned to the Bridge in 2019 and for three years worked as our technical and performance advisor, providing guidance and support on all football matters throughout the club. The Brazilian defender enjoyed two stints in SW6, from 2011 to 2014 and then again from 2016 to 2019. The charismatic and ball-playing centre-back was a hit both on the pitch and off it at the Blues, winning the Champions League, two Europa Leagues, the Premier League and two FA Cups. Luiz joined Arsenal in 2019 and played in north London for two seasons, where he also added another FA Cup medal to his trophy cabinet. Gallas proved to be an excellent bit of business for Chelsea as the young defender would go on to become an integral part of the Blues side which won two Premier Leagues and a League Cup during his five years at the Bridge. Quick, strong, defensively sound and good on the ball, Gallas' quality meant he forged impressive partnerships with Marcel Desailly and John Terry when used in his preferred position of centre-back. But his outstanding versatility meant he was equally adept at playing right-back or left-back, where he spent much of his time during our 2004/05 title win. Gallas was part of the deal which brought Ashley Cole to Stamford Bridge and the France international would play regularly for the Gunners during his four years at the club, before making the move to north London rivals Tottenham. The legendary left-back made his senior debut for Arsenal in 1999 and remained at the Gunners until 2006, winning three FA Cups and two Premier League titles in that time. Cole's standing as one of - and in some fans' eyes the - best left-back in English football history grew even further at Chelsea. Good in defence and attack, with the speed to handle any winger, Cole won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League, four FA Cups and the League Cup during his time at Stamford Bridge. The fact only five clubs have won more FA Cups than Cole's seven in the competition's 150-plus-year history says a lot about his quality and he is rightly revered as one of the greatest left-backs of all time. The holding midfielder first made his mark in professional football at Le Havre before signing for Chelsea in 2005. The France international spent two seasons at the Bridge, winning both domestic cups in that time. He then moved to Arsenal in August 2007 before joining Portsmouth the following January, having even more success at Real Madrid and several other clubs. Petit joined Arsenal from French side Monaco in 1997 and spent three seasons at the club, winning the Premier League and FA Cup with the Gunners while also lifting the World Cup and European Championship with France. After spending the next season at Barcelona, the Frenchman returned to the English capital in 2001 to join the Blues. Petit spent three years at the Bridge but unfortunately had to retire through knee injury six months after leaving the Blues. A true Arsenal legend, Rocastle was an integral part of the Gunners team which won the First Division - now the Premier League - title in 1989 and 1991. After spells at high-flying Leeds United and then Manchester City, former Blues manager Glenn Hoddle brought 'Rocky' to Stamford Bridge in 1994 and the midfielder was still able to make an impact during his initial couple of years at the club, despite having to manage knee injuries. Rocastle sadly passed away at the age of just 33 in 2001 due to non-Hodgkin lymphoma but his infectious personality, quality on the pitch and outstanding 'one-for-all' mentality mean his name is still sung from the Emirates stands even to this day. Little was known about Fabregas when he moved to Arsenal as a teenager but he would become one of the best centre midfielders of the Premier League era and a serial winner. Fabregas may have only lifted one FA Cup during his eight years at Arsenal but he was a key part of the Gunners team which reached the Champions League final and his talent took him back to Barcelona, where he enjoyed a trophy-laden three years. A switch to Chelsea in 2014 saw the trophies keep coming as he played a big part in us winning two Premier Leagues, one FA Cup and a League Cup before departing for Monaco five years later. Benayoun joined Chelsea in 2010 after successful spells at the likes of West Ham United and Liverpool. The attacking midfielder struggled to cement a regular spot at Chelsea during his three years at the club but still managed to claim a Europa League winner's medal in 2013. Although he spent longer at the Bridge, Benayoun actually played more games for Arsenal during his one-season loan at the Gunners in the 2011/12 campaign. Willian enjoyed a hugely influential seven years at Chelsea between 2013 and 2020, lifting the Europa League, two Premier Leagues, one FA Cup and one League Cup while at the Bridge. The manner of his arrival at Chelsea, not to mention his performances while in Blue, means his name is still sung in the stands at Stamford Bridge. Willian spent a season at Arsenal following his departure from Chelsea and after a year back in his native Brazil, returned to the Premier League and West London for two successful seasons with Fulham before joining Olympiacos in the summer of 2024. A second spell at Fulham and a stint back in Brazil with Gremio since followed, before he left the side in the summer of 2026. The striker burst on to the Premier League scene following his move to Arsenal while still 17 years old and quickly established himself as one of the most exciting talents in Europe. After helping the Gunners to the league and cup double in 1998 and claiming the Premier League's Golden Boot the following season, he made a big-money move to Real Madrid and re-joined Paris Saint-Germain before returning to the Premier League with a loan to Liverpool in 2001. Further spells at English sides and in Turkey were to follow before Anelka joined Chelsea in January 2008, and helped the Blues reach the Champions League final later that season.
